brief: Brent is on track to finish the week ~15% down on hopes of a US-Iran diplomatic breakthrough, but UBS's energy sales desk argues this is mispriced: Iran's seven conditions (sanctions lifted, frozen funds released, naval blockade ended, no renewed attacks, US troop withdrawal, reparations, control of the Strait of Hormuz) make a near-term deal unlikely, so a return to military conflict damaging regional energy infrastructure is more probable than diplomatic progress. UBS also flags EU integrated equities already imply ~$70/b oil, leaving room for further correction, and disputes other brokers' view that falling demand pushed the oil market into surplus in October. Separately, UBS's trading desk recaps a historic Thursday US equity rout (Nasdaq -6.36%, S&P -4.36%, SOX -12%, $2.3T of tech market cap and $185B of billionaire wealth erased) that began as AI-led selling and broadened into a wider positioning unwind, lifting Treasuries, gold and WTI; the desk's US strategy team flags forced fund selling and possible further retail selling into the weekend, with Asia following overnight. UBS expects a firmer-than-consensus October jobs report but calls the strength technical, not a real labor-demand improvement. The note closes with a roundup of energy-company 3Q26 earnings and sector news items.
